The owner approved the runtime budget.
context:
Filed 2026-11-20 from the adversarial review of the scale-factor and TPC-DI remediation work (PRs #4298-#4385 and benchbox-site #178-#210).

Owner decisions 2026-11-20 (choice dialog, 13:25Z). gate_measure = "measure-then-ask": run the nine SF 1 gate runs locally through `make heavy-run`, then one throwaway probe pull request; bring the table; the owner approves the budget before arming. gate_utils = "seed-loader-and-limit": gate only `coffeeshop_seed_loader.py`; keep the rest as a documented limit. arming = "agent-when-gates-met": once every gate on a pull request's items is met, run `make pr-arm` once, no loop, and report. threads = "after-rereview": push the fix and reply; a thread is resolved only after the bot has reviewed the new head and not raised the finding again, and not by the agent.

## Guardrails (accepted by the owner, 2026-11-20)
The agent never posts a stand-in review, resolves a review thread, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. It arms with `make pr-arm` once per pull request and reports the result. Subagents are read-only. Any limit, default, threshold or label text is shown to the owner before it is committed. A blocked step stops this item; the agent moves to the next item and does not work around the block.
description:
## Problem
The gate's measuring path (`run_smoke`: `benchbox run` at SF 1 on DuckDB, then sizing the datagen tree) has never run in CI; the job was always skipped. The baseline was produced by calling generator classes directly, a different counting path, so agreement is unproven for tpcdi, write_primitives, transaction_primitives and vector_search, and it is unknown whether each benchmark's power phase passes on DuckDB at SF 1. The 45-minute job timeout and 1500 s per-benchmark timeout have no measurement or owner approval. generator-volume-changes-pass-pr-ci-unchecked-20261112 requires a mutation probe that fails required CI, a measured runtime cost and owner approval of the required check and budget.

## Change
Run the gate for each of the nine benchmarks through `make heavy-run` and record measured bytes against the baseline, wall time and peak memory. Report each disagreement with both byte counts and its cause; the owner picks which side changes. Then run a mutation probe on a throwaway branch pull request that multiplies one generator's output and confirm `core` fails.

## Decision gates
The owner approves opening the probe pull request (a hosted write with about 45 minutes of CI) and the `MERGE_GATE_EXEMPTIONS` entry for generator-volume. The owner approves the measured runtime budget and the check being required before #4322 is armed. A benchmark whose power phase cannot pass on DuckDB at SF 1 is reported to the owner, not dropped from the gate silently. The throwaway probe pull request is closed unmerged.

## Verification rubric
Pass: a nine-row table (benchmark, baseline bytes, measured bytes, drift, seconds, peak GiB) with heavy-run log paths; the probe pull request's failing `core` run URL; the owner's budget approval recorded on this item.

## Guardrails
- Any limit, default, threshold or label id or text is shown to the owner before it is committed. Briefs quote owner answers verbatim; questions to the owner carry no preselected answer.
- The implementer replies on review threads and leaves resolving them to the reviewer or the owner, unless the owner says otherwise (AGENTS.md asks agents to resolve benchbox-oracle threads on soundness paths; the owner has been asked which applies).
- Hosted writes (merge, close, disable or enable auto-merge, workflow dispatch, remote branch delete) only as the repository's close-out procedure or the owner's word for that pull request allows; never raw `gh pr merge` in core.
- No polling loop around `make pr-arm`, no `--no-verify`, no stand-in review unless the owner names the PR and head unprompted. Push only after `make pr-preflight` exits 0 on the exact head.
- No worktree takeover while another session may be working; no tracker write from a server that reports a stale version; never chain `git stash` with `git stash pop`.
- Heavy work runs only through `make heavy-run` or a lock-taking entry point, one run at a time.
- Status reports state only what merged and what was verified, with the evidence.
